rulings.Case Title: GERMAIN MARTIN LEE INGALLS VS. GERMAN MOTORS CORPORATION DBA BMW OF SAN FRANCISCO ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Motion To Compel Further Responses To Request For Production Of Documents, Set One, From Defendant Bmw Of North America, Llc; Request For Sanctions; Declaration Of Michael K. Teiman (Motions)
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 1. Plaintiff Germain Ingalls' motion to compel further responses to his set one document requests from defendant BMW of North America, Inc. and for monetary sanctions is denied. All of the document requests which Ingalls seeks to compel further responses lack discovery relevance and are overbroad. Ingalls fails to present facts why information about airbags other than the airbag in his vehicle and those included in Recall 15V-318 is reasonably calculated to lead to the discovery of admissible evidence or will assist with his trial preparation, especially given the huge number and variety of Takata airbags, the massive scope of the recalls of Takata airbags, and the many different claimed defects in those airbags that did not involve either the PSDI-4 inflator or an incident with an airbag shooting shrapnel. While Ingalls' refusal to narrow the scope of his document requests lacks subsantial justification, no sanctions are awarded against Ingalls or his counsel because BMW does not provide any information about the expense it incurred in opposing this motion. rulings.Case Title: MARIANGEL AGUILAR ET AL VS. SHORT STORY, INC., A DELAWARE CORPORATION ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Motion To Compel Further Responses To And Compliance With Demand For Inspection Of Tangible Things, Set One; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities; Request For Monetary Sanctions (Ccp 2031.310, 202 (Motions)
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 2. Plaintiff Mariangel Aguilar's motion to compel further responses to and compliance with her set one demand for inspection of tangible things and for monetary sanctions is granted. No later than July 24, 2026 defendant Short Story, Inc. must a) serve verified code-complaint further responses without objections to the set one demand for inspection of tangible things, and b) comply fully with that inspection demand including producing the "Receiving Laptop" and related items to DataChasers, Inc. for forensic imaging per the inspection protocol. No later than August 7 Short Story must also pay reasonable monetary sanctions of $5,010 to Aguilar. Aguilar's counsel sufficiently met and conferred regarding production of the "Receiving Laptop" for forensic imaging by Aguilar's chosen vendor. As of the filing of this motion, notwithstanding that it requested more time to review Garcia's declarations, it was apparent that Short Story was unwilling to comply with the inspection demand and subsequent events have borne that out. Aguilar has shown good for her inspection demand and the declaration from Short Story's chosen vendor, while casting some doubt on the utility of the inspection demand, does not remove the good cause for that demand. The statements made by Mr. Garcia about what occurred on the date of his termination sufficiently support Aguilar's request to "verify" that all non-privileged responsive documents on the Receiving Laptop were produced. Short Story's resistance to Aguilar's chosen vendor imaging of the Receiving Laptop lacks substantial justification. The materials that were assertedly transferred to that laptop are, if as described by Garcia, highly probative. The purposes of civil discovery -- including both fairness and equal access to claimed relevant evidence -- requires that Aguilar not be required to accept the declaration from Short Story's chosen vendor without having an opportunity for its chosen vendor to image the laptop. rulings.Case Title: BIANCA BABOR VS. AIRBNB, INC., A DELAWARE CORPORATION ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 6. Defendants Airbnb, Inc. and Airbnb RPG, Inc.'s motion to compel arbitration and stay proceedings is granted. This case is stayed pending the conclusion of arbitration proceedings. By the declaration of Greg Anderson submitted with the moving papers, defendants satisfied their initial burden of showing that there is an agreement between defendants and plaintiff Bianca Babor requiring arbitration of the claims alleged by Babor. Nothing in Babor's declaration or in her opposition memorandum showed that the arbitration agreement in defendants' Terms of Service is invalid. Since defendants provided evidence that Babor agreed to the Terms of Service when she signed up for defendants' services in 2017 and on multiple occasions thereafter, Babor's failure to read the Terms of Service is not a basis to deny this motion. (B.D. v. Blizzard Entertainment, Inc. (2022) 76 Cal. App. 5th 931, 943) The recent decision in Wilkins v. Cruise (First District Court of Appeal February 14, 2026) 2026 WL 2029446 sets out two questions for resolving arguments whether a user of services signed up for on-line, as Babor claims, lacked inquiry notice of the arbitration agreement in the Terms of Service. As in Wilkins, since the answer to both questions is yes, Babor's lack of notice arguments fail. The first question is whether defendants' on-line processes provided sufficient notice that a user was agreeing to the hyperlinked Terms of Service. Much like the on-line processes in Wilkins, defendants' on-line processes provided ample notice to a user that when she was signing up for defendants' services, she was agreeing to the hyperlinked Terms of Service. (Anderson 2/2/26 Dec. Exs. C-E). The second question is whether the Terms of Service provided sufficient notice of the arbitration agreement therein. Also, like Wilkins, the first page of the hyperlinked Terms of Service when Babor signed up for defendants' services highlighted the arbitration agreement and the arbitration agreement itself unambiguously and clearly stated that a user had to arbitrate her disputes with defendants and was waiving her right to a jury trial. (Id. Ex. F.) For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. rulings.Case Title: JANE DOE VS. PAT KULETO ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 8. 1 - Defendant Pat Kuleto's demurrer to the seventh cause of action for sexual harassment in plaintiff Esmeralda Ortiz's first amended complaint is sustained without leave to amend. In her seventh cause of action for sexual harassment in violaton of Civil Code 51.9 Ortiz alleges that at all relevant times she was employed by Kuleto. That allegation forecloses her attempt to seek redress against Kuleto under section 51.9. In Hughes v. Pair (2009) 46 Cal. 4th 1035, 1044-1046 repeatedly and unequivocally refers to section 51.9 as covering alleged sexually related misconduct in "relationships outside the workplace" as distinct from sexually related misconduct in the workplace. Since there is no reasonable possibility that Ortiz is able to allege a viable section 51.9 claim, Kulelto's demurrer to that claim is sustained without leave to amend. rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Moiton To Transfer Action And For Sanctions; Memornadum Of Points And Authorities; Declarations Of Martin R. Berman, Alicia Salling And Matthew Corvo, M.D. In Support Thereof; Request For Sanctions In The Amount Of $7,560
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 8. 2 - Defendant Pat Kuleto's motion to transfer action and for sanctions is denied. Paragraphs 48-53 of plaintiff Esmeralda Ortiz's first amended complaint alleges that she was sexually harassed in San Francisco. Those paragraphs are sufficient for venue to lie in San Francisco per the FEHA venue statute providing for venue "in any county ... in any county in which the unlawful practice is alleged to have been committed." (Government Code 12965(c)(3)). The portion of Kuleto's motion based on asserted inconvenience of witnesses is premature since Kuleto has not yet filed an answer.
